notes: Parity with clab_data_collection_template v1. Process-based L3 variant deferred to a later catalog version. The UI is generated from this file: adding, removing or re-staging a dimension requires no code change.

pilot_fields.label: Attribution category
pilot_fields.help: Pre-filled from pilot type; override only with a reason.

stages.label: Ideation
stages.instructions: Plan the impact evaluation: state hypotheses, sketch the counterfactual and identify available data sources. Fill what is knowable now; leave the rest blank.

stages.label: Design
stages.instructions: Complete Level 1 (Design & Relevance), confirm the counterfactuals still hold, record baselines for Level 3 and document lessons learned during ideation and design.

stages.label: Implementation
stages.instructions: Capture Level 2 (costs, timeliness, benchmarking), document the process and record mid-term indicators.

stages.label: Evaluation
stages.instructions: Complete Level 3 with post-treatment data and attribute results. Sustainability of results is assessed here.

dimensions.name: Relevance
dimensions.definition: The extent to which the intervention objectives and design respond to beneficiaries', global, country and partner/institution needs, policies and priorities, and continue to do so if circumstances change.
guiding_questions: Does the pilot address a real and prioritized problem identified by the community or local government?
Is it consistent with IDB country strategy, the SDGs or the Paris Agreement?
Does the design include analysis of marginalized or vulnerable groups (leave no one behind)?

dimensions.name: Sustainability of design
dimensions.definition: Whether the design model provides mechanisms for the continuation of benefits once the LAB's involvement ends. The full assessment of sustainability (observed benefits) is conducted at Level 3.
guiding_questions: Does the design contemplate how continuity will be financed without extraordinary IDB resources?
Does the counterpart have the technical and operational capacity to maintain the intervention?
Does the design anticipate climate, social or institutional risks that could affect continuity?

dimensions.name: Coherence
dimensions.definition: The compatibility of the intervention with other interventions in a country, sector or institution: internal coherence (other IDB actions and norms) and external coherence (other interventions in the same country).
guiding_questions: Does the pilot complement other IDB operations in the same city or country?
Was coordination established with local government, civil society or other donors?
Were there similar interventions in the territory? Were they taken into account?
Is the intervention consistent with international commitments the country or IDB have signed?

dimensions.name: Cultural localization
guiding_questions: Does the intervention adequately engage with the practices, identities and ways of life of the local community?
Was it co-created with or validated by territorial stakeholders?

dimensions.name: Relationship with existing regulations
guiding_questions: Does the intervention comply with applicable urban, environmental, construction and safety regulations?
If not, does it clearly identify the adjustments required?

dimensions.name: User experience & continuous feedback
guiding_questions: Is the prototype useful from the perspective of the citizens who use it? In what ways?
What can be improved?
Is there a mechanism for continuous feedback, or was feedback collected once?

dimensions.name: Construction system
dimensions.applies_note: Only for urban interventions with a material/built component.
guiding_questions: Is the proposed construction system cost-effective?
Does it use local inputs and capacities?
Does it allow for viable community management during and after works?

dimensions.name: Disaggregated costs
dimensions.definition: Comprehensive budget split into capital expenditure (one-time investments to create or install the intervention) and operating expenditure (recurring costs to operate and sustain it). All amounts in USD. Totals are computed, never typed.
dimensions.currency_rule: Report in USD. If the source figure is in another currency, record the original amount and currency in the optional cost breakdown and enter the USD equivalent here.

fields.label: Construction and physical installation
fields.help: Civil works, fixed infrastructure, structural materials

fields.label: Durable equipment
fields.help: Sensors, hardware, vehicles, tools, durable furnishings

fields.label: Initial training and capacity-building
fields.help: One-time training that installs capacity in the counterpart

fields.label: Other capex
fields.help: Sum here any one-time cost not covered by the categories above; describe it in the notes.

fields.label: Other opex
fields.help: Sum here any recurring cost not covered above; describe it in the notes.

fields.label: Who paid for what
fields.help: e.g. IDB financed surveys only; vehicles funded by a third party

dimensions.name: Timeliness
guiding_questions: Was the project delivered within the planned timeframe?
If not, what were the main factors affecting timeliness?

dimensions.name: Benchmarking
guiding_questions: Is the project cost-effective relative to alternatives?
Are there similar interventions against which to compare the cost per unit result?

dimensions.name: Effectiveness
dimensions.definition: The extent to which the intervention achieved, or is expected to achieve, its objectives and results, including any differential results across groups.
guiding_questions: What proportion of the pilot's stated objectives was achieved?
Were there unplanned achievements?
Were the results equitable? Did benefits reach the most vulnerable groups the intervention sought to serve?
What contextual, design or implementation conditions explain the outcomes?

dimensions.name: Impact
dimensions.repeatable_note: One record per impact hypothesis. A pilot may have as many hypotheses as it needs; add them at ideation or later.
dimensions.definition: The extent to which the intervention has generated or is expected to generate significant positive or negative, intended or unintended, higher-level effects. Where evidence is limited or inferred, say so explicitly rather than leaving the field empty.
guiding_questions: Were changes observed in the urban or social environment (mobility, temperature, safety, social cohesion, land values)?
Did anything change in institutional capacity? Did the counterpart adopt new practices, tools or processes?
Were there unintended effects, positive or negative, on groups not initially considered?
Is there a Theory of Change or causal chain linking the pilot to expected effects?

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.help: Expected direct or indirect benefit, stated as a testable claim.

fields.label: Counterfactual
fields.help: What would have happened without the pilot, and how it is approximated (control area, synthetic scenario, pre/post). Not the null hypothesis.

fields.label: Unit of analysis
fields.help: Block, street segment, census tract, buffer, classroom, household…

fields.label: Identification strategy
fields.help: Preferred: DiD. Pre/post without control and qualitative are valid as long as they are declared.

dimensions.name: Sustainability of results
dimensions.definition: The extent to which the net benefits of the intervention continue or are likely to continue after the LAB withdraws.
guiding_questions: Is there evidence or indication that benefits continue after the LAB's involvement ended?
What risks threaten continuity (financial, political, environmental, social)?
Has the local government institutionalized the intervention or made concrete plans to do so?

dimensions.name: Design lessons
guiding_questions: What did the team learn during the design process?
What design decisions were taken, what tensions emerged and what trade-offs were resolved?
Which particularities of the design are expected to make the intervention more effective, and why?

dimensions.name: Implementation lessons
guiding_questions: What operational, technical or institutional learnings emerged during execution?
How did the counterpart experience working with the LAB? What burden did the process impose on them?

dimensions.name: Scaling lessons
guiding_questions: Under what conditions could this solution be replicated or scaled?
What adjustments would it require?

dimensions.name: Evaluation lessons
guiding_questions: What data should have been collected from the start?
What methodology would be more appropriate in a subsequent phase?

dimensions.name: Qualitative co-benefits
guiding_questions: What sensory, psychological or relational improvements did participants report that are not easily quantifiable?
At design stage: which co-benefits are expected? At evaluation: which were observed?

stage_completion.rule: Completing a stage stores a snapshot of every field editable at that stage and marks the stage complete. Fields remain editable afterwards; the UI warns before saving a change to a completed stage.
stage_completion.required_for_completion: All core dimensions editable at the stage must have a status (filled, no_evidence or not_applicable). Non-core dimensions may be left empty.
